expectations.text: Uses cdkTrapFocus or CdkTrapFocus directive from @angular/cdk/a11y for focus trapping
expectations.evidence: The template applies `cdkTrapFocus cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture="true"` to the panel div, and the component imports `A11yModule` from `@angular/cdk/a11y`.

expectations.text: Dialog has role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' or uses the native <dialog> element
expectations.evidence: The component's `host` object sets `role: 'dialog'` and `'aria-modal': 'true'` directly on the host element.

expectations.text: Focus moves to the dialog on open (autoFocus or programmatic focus)
expectations.evidence: `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture="true"` on the panel div moves focus into the trap as soon as it is attached to the DOM. `cdkFocusInitial` on the Cancel button designates the exact element that receives focus.

expectations.text: Escape key closes the dialog via keyboard event handler
expectations.evidence: The host binding `'(keydown.escape)': 'close.emit("cancelled")'` emits the close output when Escape is pressed, triggering the service cleanup that destroys the component.

expectations.text: Focus returns to the trigger element after dialog closes
expectations.evidence: The service captures `document.activeElement` as `triggerElement` before calling `createComponent`, then calls `triggerElement?.focus()` in the `cleanup` function after destroying the component.

expectations.text: Background content uses the inert attribute or aria-hidden='true'
expectations.evidence: `setBodyChildrenInert()` iterates over all direct `<body>` children except the dialog host and sets `child.setAttribute('inert', '')` on each. The attributes are removed in `cleanup`.
`changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` is present in the `@Component` decorator of `ConfirmationDialogComponent`. The usage example component (`DeleteItemComponent`) also sets `OnPush`.

expectations.text: Has aria-labelledby or aria-label for the dialog title
expectations.evidence: The host sets `'[attr.aria-labelledby]': '"confirmation-dialog-title"'`, and the `<h2>` in the template carries `id="confirmation-dialog-title"`, forming a complete labelling relationship.

claims.claim: Focus moves to the first focusable element (Cancel) when the dialog opens via cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture + cdkFocusInitial
claims.evidence: Both directives are present in the template: `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture="true"` on the panel and `cdkFocusInitial` on the Cancel button.

claims.claim: Background content is inert — the service sets the `inert` attribute on all `<body>` children outside the dialog host
claims.evidence: `setBodyChildrenInert()` loops over `document.body.children`, skips the host element, and calls `child.setAttribute('inert', '')` on the rest.

claims.claim: Stacking multiple dialogs works correctly — each invocation independently marks and restores inert targets
claims.evidence: The design note describes the intended behaviour, but no code test or proof is present in the output. The logic appears structurally sound (each `confirm()` call has its own `inertTargets` closure), but runtime correctness cannot be confirmed from the static output alone.

claims.claim: LiveAnnouncer is used as a reliable fallback for screen readers that do not announce dynamically injected dialogs
claims.evidence: `LiveAnnouncer` is injected in the service and called with `announce('Dialog opened: ...')` before the component is rendered, and `announce('Dialog closed')` in `cleanup`.

suggestions.assertion: Focus moves to the dialog on open (autoFocus or programmatic focus)
suggestions.reason: The assertion passes on the presence of `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture`, but does not verify that focus lands on a specific, meaningful element. WAI-ARIA APG recommends initial focus on the least-destructive action (Cancel) for confirmation dialogs. A stronger assertion would check that `cdkFocusInitial` is placed on Cancel (not Confirm), making the assertion sensitive to accidentally dangerous focus placement.

No assertion checks that the `inert` attribute is cleaned up after the dialog closes. Leaking `inert` on body children after close would break the app silently, and none of the current assertions would catch it.

No assertion verifies that `aria-describedby` is present for the dialog body text. The WAI-ARIA dialog pattern recommends both `aria-labelledby` (title) and `aria-describedby` (message). The output provides both, but only the labelledby relationship is asserted.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions are meaningful and would fail for a naive implementation. The three suggestions above cover gaps around focus-target correctness, cleanup correctness, and the aria-describedby relationship — outcomes the eval author would likely want to catch.
